reason: The cited evidence shows single-atom Pd on high-entropy oxide (E4) and single-atom Pt in high-entropy alloy nanoparticles (E1, E3), but none demonstrates atomically dispersed Pt on a high-entropy oxide support, nor scalable synthesis of such a system, nor the claimed >70% Pt reduction with maintained activity under automotive exhaust cycling.
premises: Single-atom Pt can be stabilized on high-entropy oxide supports via defect anchoring.
High-entropy oxide supports provide enhanced metal-support interactions and charge transfer that optimize catalytic activity.
Scalable synthesis methods can produce atomically dispersed Pt on high-entropy oxides.
Single-atom Pt catalysts on high-entropy oxides resist sintering under high-temperature cycling.
Single-atom Pt catalysts achieve high turnover frequency with >70% reduction in Pt loading compared to nanoparticle catalysts.
